instances.note: instance ids, not used by STCOcc occupancy-only training/eval

flow.note: real per-voxel flow vector; read only when load_flow=True

multi_scale.generated_by: tools/generate_ms_occ.py / tools/generate_ms_occ_parallel.py (identical algorithm, bit-identical output, verified this session)
multi_scale.downsample_method: majority-vote per block with a 95%-empty threshold (downsample_label/downsample_mask in generate_ms_occ.py), NOT naive nearest/average -- empty_cls_idx is free_index (16 for openocc, 17 for occ3d)
keys_written: mask_camera (occ3d only, if source has it)
mask_lidar (occ3d only, if source has it)
multi_scale.known_placeholder: the 'flow' key in every labels_1_X.npz (both Occ3D's and OpenOcc's, this is upstream Ref/STCOcc_ori behavior, not a local bug) is literally the downsampled SEMANTIC LABEL array reused under the 'flow' key, not a real downsampled flow vector field. Confirmed never consumed downstream by the detector at any scale (get_flow_loss only ever reads full-resolution kwargs['voxel_flows']). The new load_flow=False path in LoadOccGTFromFileOpenOcc never reads this key at all, so this placeholder cannot affect the occupancy-only baseline.
multi_scale.class_preservation_verified: downsampled class set is always a subset of the full-resolution class set (checked this session on real generated OpenOcc files: research_openocc/tests/test_openocc_baseline.py T9); bit-identical to the single-threaded reference function on sampled tokens.
multi_scale.coverage_openocc: generated this session for all 28130 train + 6019 val samples via tools/generate_ms_occ_parallel.py (did not exist before; this was the single blocking reason stcocc_r50_704x256_16f_openocc_12e.py could not even start training -- see audit.md section 3.5)
